items.title: Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Clarence Williams' and 'Splendid Platt' as people who came from the same region ('down that way') but does not describe a personal interaction or professional relationship with Clarence Platt.

ctx.x: Yeah, in the country. No, he used to play in brass band. Up there, they had a brass band? Yeah, yeah, one of them in Yolens, Louisiana brass band. So I don't know how my brother started, but he gave me these sticks. So that's how I picked it up myself. So my first plane was, he used to work for Dennis, a Dr. Graw in New Orleans, and he used to go down below the city in Plaquemine Parish, I think you call it that, with a fellow by the name of Till. He used to hire the fellows out of New Orleans and go to play down…

So one time, my brother couldn't get off. Well, excuse me, do you know Zeb's real name, his last name? No, all I knew was he's Zeb. No, I never could think of his last name, Clarence Platt. I believe Professor Minetta, who was here last night, said something like L-E-N-O-I-R.

Well it could be, but we always called him Zeb or Zeb. So he couldn't make the trip. And in the meantime, I still was wearing short pants. So my brother asked me, he said, do you think if I let you go to my place, could you make it? He said, well, I don't know, I'll try. So I had to borrow a pair of long pants to put on. So I went in his place, the fellow, his boy was, he played clarinet and guitar. His first name was Koyko. Oh yes. Yeah. He talked about the California years. Yeah, he died, you know. So I went in…
